title: Quote attachments: S3 storage adapter and endpoints
objective: Quotes support multiple validated file attachments stored in S3-compatible object storage behind a configurable adapter, streamed through the API with authorization and audit (spec FR-48, A-4, §16).
scope: IObjectStorage + S3ObjectStorage (any S3-compatible endpoint; MinIO locally)
Upload/download/delete endpoints with type, magic-number, and per-tenant size validation
implementation_details: Application/Abstractions/IObjectStorage.cs: PutAsync(key, stream, contentType), OpenReadAsync(key), DeleteAsync(key); Infrastructure/Storage/S3ObjectStorage.cs using AWSSDK.S3 (Apache-2.0) with ServiceURL + ForcePathStyle from config, credentials from Vault; bucket from config (quoteiq-attachments)
Liquibase 120-attachments: quote_attachments per spec §11.3 (storage_key text, removed_by/at soft delete)

Features/Quotes/Attachments: UploadAttachmentCommand: allow-list content types image/png, image/jpeg, application/pdf, application/msword, application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document; FileSignatureValidator checks magic numbers match declared type (PNG/JPG/PDF signatures; DOCX=ZIP PK header, DOC=OLE header); size <= tenant max_attachment_mb; storage key pattern t{tenantId}/quotes/{quoteId}/{attachmentId}_{sanitizedFileName}; DownloadAttachmentQuery streams with Content-Disposition attachment and stored content type; RemoveAttachmentCommand soft-deletes row and deletes object; add/remove audited
Closed-quote rule: upload/remove on closed quotes requires Quotes.CorrectClosed (FR-48/FR-49)
compose MinIO init already creates bucket (T-001); integration tests use Testcontainers MinIO

findings.description: Upload endpoint lacks a request-body-size limit below the framework default (~30MB Kestrel/multipart). The per-tenant cap IS enforced (UploadAttachmentCommandHandler checks IFormFile.Length against MaxAttachmentMb before the S3 PUT, so no oversize object persists), but a file over the tenant cap yet under the framework default is fully buffered (spooled to disk) before the handler rejects it. Minor because the endpoint is authenticated + Quotes.Update-gated (not anonymous), the ceiling is bounded, and large bodies spool to disk not memory.
findings.recommendation: Add an endpoint-level request-size limit aligned to a maximum sane tenant cap (e.g. RequestSizeLimit / MultipartBodyLengthLimit) so oversize uploads are rejected pre-buffering.
findings.resolution: Verified fix iteration 2 (evaluator audit). New RequestBodySizeLimitFilter (IEndpointFilter setting IHttpMaxRequestBodySizeFeature.MaxRequestBodySize before the handler/IFormFile binding) applied via .WithRequestBodySizeLimit(25MB) on the upload endpoint; 25MB = 20MB MaxSupportedTenantCapMb x 1.25 headroom, narrower than Kestrel's ~28.6MB default so grossly-oversize rejects pre-buffering; per-tenant handler cap UNCHANGED. Untested-framework-ceiling ACCEPTED: WebApplicationFactory/TestServer has no Kestrel/IIS transport so IHttpMaxRequestBodySizeFeature isn't enforced there - a ceiling test would be meaningless; the handler over-cap 422 test covers the functional path. Residual (MaxAttachmentMb unbounded) tracked as info F-066.

findings.description: DOCX shares the 50 4B 03 04 PK ZIP header, so a .zip/.xlsx/.pptx declared as DOCX passes the four-byte signature check. Documented in the validator XML doc. Does not weaken AC-047 (allow-list still blocks dangerous declared types; residual confusion only among non-executable OOXML/ZIP formats; served as forced-content-type attachment).
findings.recommendation: Optional follow-up: unzip + inspect [Content_Types].xml for true DOCX validation. ACCEPTED as-is; not required.

findings.description: AC-077 / spec section 16 wording is 'extension + magic-number check'; the handler validates the declared Content-Type + magic number but NOT the filename extension itself. Security intent is met (bytes proven to be an allow-listed type, forced content-type attachment, no execution/XSS vector), so this is a literal AC-wording gap.
findings.evidence: UploadAttachmentCommandHandler.cs:95-112 (content-type + magic number, no extension check).
findings.recommendation: Add a filename-extension check consistent with the allow-listed content type (belt-and-suspenders) to satisfy the AC-077 literal 'extension + magic-number' wording, keeping the content-type+magic-number validation.
findings.resolution: Verified fix iteration 2 (evaluator audit). FileSignatureValidator.AllowedExtensionsByContentType + IsExtensionAllowed; UploadAttachmentCommandHandler:107-111 extracts Path.GetExtension from the pre-sanitization filename -> 422 ATTACHMENT_EXTENSION_MISMATCH on mismatch. THREE-WAY agreement enforced without weakening: content-type allow-list (:97-100 unchanged) + extension (:108 new/additive) + magic-number bytes (:120-125 unchanged) must all pass. Tests: theory (6 accept, 5 mismatch reject, 1 not-allow-listed reject) + integration Upload_WhenExtensionMismatchesDeclaredContentType_ShouldReturn422 (valid PNG bytes + image/png + named logo.jpg -> 422, isolates the extension leg). Satisfies AC-077 literal wording.

findings.description: No dedicated unit test for AttachmentStorageKey.Sanitize, a path-traversal / S3-key-injection security boundary. The sanitizer is correct on inspection but unlocked by tests.
findings.evidence: FileSignatureValidatorTests.cs covers only the signature validator; no Sanitize tests.
findings.recommendation: Add adversarial-filename unit cases (../../etc/passwd, ..\evil, control chars, empty-after-strip, leading dot) asserting the sanitized key has no path separators/traversal.
findings.resolution: Verified fix iteration 2. AttachmentStorageKeySanitizeTests 6 adversarial cases (unix traversal->passwd, windows ..\..\evil.png->evil.png, control chars->bad__name.pdf, empty-after-strip->attachment, leading-dot .htaccess->htaccess, normal logo.png) each asserting no /, no \, no .., + exact expected output. InternalsVisibleTo QuoteIQ.Application.Tests added (AttachmentStorageKey is internal) - test-enablement only, no production surface.

findings.description: The upload audit row (quote_attachment.uploaded) is written but never asserted by a test (only the remove audit is).
findings.evidence: UploadAttachmentCommandHandler.cs:148 (audit write); no test asserts it.
findings.recommendation: Assert the quote_attachment.uploaded audit row in the round-trip test.
findings.resolution: Verified fix iteration 2. UploadDownloadRoundTrip now asserts exactly one quote_attachment.uploaded audit row (EntityType==quote_attachment, EntityId==uploaded.Id, Action==quote_attachment.uploaded) via Assert.Single, mirroring the remove-audit assertion.

findings.description: TenantSettings.MaxAttachmentMb has no enforced upper bound in UpdateBusinessRulesValidator (only >0), so it can drift above the 20MB (25MB request) framework ceiling and silently break legitimate over-20MB uploads with a confusing framework-level rejection instead of the clean ATTACHMENT_OVER_SIZE_CAP 422. The residual is documented in code and lies outside the documented supported range (A-4 default 10MB, supported to 20MB).
findings.recommendation: Add a MaxAttachmentMb <= MaxSupportedTenantCapMb upper-bound validation so the tenant cap and framework ceiling cannot diverge into a broken state. Informational; belongs to the business-rules validator (T-010/T-016 territory). Non-blocking.
